answers.goals: Keep extending.md's engine/content boundary structural: core (checks/, mount/, engine/, .github/, the top-level docs, and the shared engine modules under packs/ and skills/) must never name a specific pack or skill — packs and skills are discovered content, and a core file citing one couples the engine to its content. One rule per namespace (packs/*, skills/*); reviewed inherent couplings live in each rule's except. migrations/ is deliberately NOT core here: a migration record is a dated one-off that exists to move the fleet off a specific pack's old shape, so naming that pack is its purpose, not a coupling — and records accumulate as dated folders, one per change, which no path-keyed exception list should have to chase.

accept.reason: the per-project-scheduling DESIGN/MIGRATION pair is the historical record of migration #394 — it names the central routine and planner files this migration deleted precisely because deleting them is what it records; rewriting those names would falsify the record, so its inbound-reference dangling is deliberate and permanent

the engine's file-set builder deliberately imports the consumer-layout constant SHARED_SUBDIR (beside LOCAL_PACKS_SUBDIR in engine/pack_loader/pack-registry.mjs — core machinery per extending.md, not a specific pack) so the shared-mount sweep exclusion and the vendor writer share one definition; the cross-tree reach is inherent, not a misplacement

the canon-side migration registry deliberately builds on the vendored sync surface in the engine lib (engine/checks/helpers/active-migrations.mjs — the home pack-independence mandates, since pack checks consult migrationActive and packs import only the engine surface); one definition, re-exported for canon callers, so the cross-tree reach is inherent, not a misplacement

an update flow is by definition the composition of the trees it moves between — the vendor-set computation it lays down, the engine surface it replaces, the migration registry it runs and the wiring it converges — so every import it has crosses a tree boundary; that reach IS the module, and putting it inside any one of those trees would either ship canon-internal machinery to every member or hide the flow inside the thing it operates on

the two compatibility entry points every member still reaches by path (baselining's vendored worker runs node <canon clone>/migrations/apply.mjs and imports its registry.mjs, and that worker is only as new as the member's last converge) — they exist to forward to the real machinery now under engine/migrations/, so reaching across is the whole of what they are, and both are deleted in Phase 5 of #768 once no member can call them

the version rule deliberately imports the scheme itself (VERSION_RE, the version reader) and the config parser from the pack's own vendored stubs, because those files are the definition: they are what runs in every site repo's .github/. Restating either canon-side would be a second copy that drifts from the code that actually bumps and reads. The reach into stubs/ is inherent to a pack whose logic ships vendored, not a misplacement

same as version-scheme.mjs: the config rule parses .github/site.config with the very parser the vendored read-site-config action runs, so the check and the pipeline can never disagree about what a valid config is

same as site-config.mjs: the pipeline-completeness rule reads .github/site.config with the vendored parser to see whether the repo declares build_vars, because the answer decides whether a pre-exporter vendored copy is stale or simply untouched. Re-parsing the config canon-side would be a second definition of a valid config that drifts from the one the runner uses

the vendor-set computation deliberately imports the import-surface facts from the engine lib (engine/checks/helpers/module-imports.mjs — the one home the pack-independence check judges against), so "what a pack may import" and "what a vendor set must carry" share one definition; the cross-tree reach is inherent, not a misplacement
